summary: Dates, party plans, honorific Korean, and a surprise guest.

lessons.goal: Say dates: months, days and years.

notes.title: Months are easy
notes.text: Korean months are just numbers + 월: 일월 (January) to 십이월 (December). Two sound changes: June is 유월 (not 육월) and October is 시월 (not 십월). Dates go big to small: 2026년 7월 10일.

notes.title: -ㄹ게요
notes.text: -ㄹ게요 / -을게요 promises your own action to the listener: 제가 할게요 ("I'll do it"), 갈게요 ("I'll go / I'm coming"). It's never used for other people's actions.

notes.title: 존댓말
notes.text: Honorific speech (존댓말) shows respect to the person you're talking ABOUT: 할머니께서 주무세요 ("Grandma is sleeping"). You never use it about yourself. Kids learn it early, and using it with elders makes a great impression.

notes.title: Birthday traditions
notes.text: Koreans eat seaweed soup (미역국) on their birthday — the soup mothers eat after giving birth, as thanks. For an elder's birthday, say 생신 축하드려요 (honorific). A 60th or 70th birthday is a big family celebration.

notes.title: Telling your story
notes.text: Life events in Korean: 태어났어요 (was born), 학교에 다녔어요 (went to school), 졸업했어요 (graduated), 취직했어요 (got a job), 결혼했어요 (got married), 이사했어요 (moved).
